Rivar the Hulk

Overview

Rivar the Hulk becomes captain after Gort. Though exceptionally strong, he admits that he dislikes fighting and is no gifted speaker. He shares his family’s secret of strength with Zak and supports him against Erfar. His later admission that the prisoner escaped shows the limits of his vigilance. [1, 2, 3]

Gort’s rebellion

The written instructions to kill Zak expose Gort’s handwriting. Confronted with the evidence, the captain turns against the authority he formerly served and declares that he will rule the village himself. He flees to gather the forest men. Erfar urges Zak to stop him before he can return; the ensuing pursuit ends Gort’s rebellion. Rivar the Hulk becomes the new captain. Unlike his predecessor, Rivar admits that he dislikes fighting, shares his family’s secret of strength and later supports Zak when suspicion finally reaches the elder. [4, 5, 6, 7, 1, 2, 8, 9]

The White Flower and Erfar’s exposure

After Gort’s fall, Erfar claims that an orc seer has cursed the village with disease and asks for a White Flower. Zak finds armed opposition waiting for him, although no villagers have yet fallen ill. Erfar blames Babur, while Babur’s earlier warning makes Zak suspect both men. Estera suggests setting a trap. Zak tells each suspect a different location for a second flower; the ambush appears at the place he gave Erfar. With Rivar’s support he confronts and imprisons the elder. An expedition report recovered from the abandoned foreign camp becomes leverage: Erfar translates its account of a concealed tunnel and its opening lever. He later escapes custody. Estera recalls that he originally arrived as an adult stranger, leaving his real purpose unresolved. [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 2, 15, 16, 3, 17, 18]
